journal: Nature Nanotechnology

title: Your battery may not be a battery
content:
Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02296-w

The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.
journal: Nature Nanotechnology

title: Interlayer sliding controls magnetism in tetralayer graphene
content:
Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02313-y

The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.
journal: Nature Nanotechnology

title: Sliding ferroelectricity scales up
content:
Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02293-z

Wafer-scale growth of a metastable rhombohedral boron nitride polytype takes sliding ferroelectricity from handcrafted structures in the laboratory towards integrated devices.
journal: Nature Nanotechnology

title: Evidence for an excitonic insulator
content:
Nature Nanotechnology, Published online: 14 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41565-026-02297-9

Using local probes and impurities on Ta2Pd3Te5 two experimental groups prove and characterize the presence of an excitonic gap via the impurity-induced breaking of excitonic pairing.
journal: Nature Nanotechnology

title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79008-4

Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Sequential protonation and deprotonation reactions govern alternating access in a Major Facilitator Superfamily proton/multidrug antiporter
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78611-9

The molecular mechanisms underlying proton-coupled drug efflux are not fully resolved. Here the authors assess the timing and mechanism of proton coupling in the multidrug transporter LmrP, a prototypical exporter of clinically relevant antibiotics and toxins.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79161-w

Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.
journal: Nature Communications

title: B7-H4‒directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors: the Phase 1/2a (BLUESTAR), first-in-human study
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78925-8

B7-H4 is a promising therapeutic target in solid tumors because of its frequent expression in cancer cells, limited normal tissue distribution, and immunosuppressive functions. In this first-in-human trial, the authors report safety and efficacy outcomes for B7-H4–directed antibody-drug conjugate AZD8205 (puxitatug samrotecan) in patients with heavily pretreated ovarian, endometrial, and breast cancers, and cholangiocarcinoma.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Observation of quantized charge accumulation in a quantum anomalous Hall system
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78306-1

The quantum anomalous Hall effect in a magnetically doped topological insulator exhibits a quantized Hall conductance. Here, the authors demonstrate an out-of-plane capacitive method that directly measures field-induced quantized charge accumulation originating from the quantized Hall conductance.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78973-0

Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) secure hardware identity but can be digitally cloned by machine-learning attacks. Here, authors report a liquid-metal PUF whose thermal keys appear only briefly during heating and are hidden among decoys, resisting both physical and digital cloning.
journal: Nature Communications

title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78532-7

Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.
journal: Nature Communications

title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
content:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78985-w

The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently.
journal: Nature Communications

title: In situ/operando Mössbauer spectroscopy in single-atom catalysis: From structure-activity relationships to dynamic mechanisms
content: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.
journal: Chem

title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
content: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.
journal: Chem

title: Using NMR to predict molecular reactivity
content: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.
journal: Chem

title: Programming hot-carrier dynamics in gold nanoclusters for high-gain photodetectors
content: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. Here, electron-donating ligands spatially separate the frontier orbitals of Au22 nanoclusters, extending hot-carrier lifetime to nanoseconds and enabling high-performance, stable photodetectors. This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.
journal: Chem

title: Ligand-protected copper nanoclusters enable room-temperature semihydrogenation of terminal alkynes
content: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.
journal: Chem

title: Selective upcycling of polyesters to dicarboxylic acids via tandem depolymerization-dehydrogenative oxidation
content: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.
journal: Chem

title: Electric rectification by a redox-conductive metal-organic framework bilayer electrode
content: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.
journal: Chem

title: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
content: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.
journal: Chem

title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
content: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.
journal: Chem

title: Accelerating solid form discovery through an expert-guided, semi-automated workflow: Modular Multiwell Devices
content: Vukotic and coworkers introduce a modular, semi-automated platform integrating solution crystallization, mechanochemistry, thermal treatment, and in situ X-ray diffraction for high-throughput pharmaceutical solid form discovery. Applied to carbamazepine, it produced multicomponent phases in 122 of 144 reactions, yielding 33 solid forms while enabling rapid screening of polymorphs, solvates, and hydrates.
journal: Chem

title: Taming transient radical couplings by preassembling organophotocatalytic dyads
content: Barham and co-workers report a sustainable, transition-metal-free platform for radical cross-couplings photocatalyzed by covalently linked, rotating organic dyads. Through weak non-covalent interactions with electronically complementary target substrates, this approach successfully generates, stabilizes, and selectively cross-couples otherwise highly reactive radical intermediates in close proximity. Facile tuning of the catalyst’s donor moiety switches mechanisms between assembly-assisted consecutive photoinduced electron transfer and ternary charge-separated EDA complexation. Non-covalent templating prevents destructive side reactions, enabling efficient, selective C–C bond formation with excellent atom economy, including late-stage pharmaceutical modifications.
journal: Chem

title: Practical and green oxidative amination of olefins
content: Allylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials, but their direct preparation often depends on costly oxidants and complex catalyst systems. We report a practical palladium-catalyzed oxidative amination of alkenes that uses air as the oxidant and does not require specialized ligands. The method converts diverse amines and alkenes into allylamines with high selectivity and can be performed on a gram scale, offering a greener route to valuable allylamine products.
journal: Chem

title: Direct O–O coupling on cation-vacancy-activated oxygen-vacancy sites of NiOOH for industrially efficient and durable OER
content: Coupled cation and oxygen vacancies in NiOOH create a distinct dual-site oxygen evolution pathway that bypasses conventional adsorbate scaling and avoids sustained bulk lattice-oxygen turnover. Direct O–O coupling through a bridged oxygen intermediate enhances intrinsic activity while preserving structural integrity, thus enabling durable operation for more than 1,600 h under industrially relevant alkaline electrolysis conditions. The work shows how defect coupling can redirect reaction mechanisms to reconcile activity and stability.
journal: Chem

title: Sustainable air purification via light-charged filters
content: A novel class of light-charged air filtration systems (LCFSs) is designed by integrating a photothermal-ferroelectric coating layer (PCL) with a polypropylene melt-blown membrane. The LCFS offers energy-efficient, light-activated surface charge generation and facilitates continuous capture of hazardous airborne particles with FE exceeding 99%, enabling sustainable air purification and anti-clogging performance. The LCFS is demonstrated as a proof of concept for indoor air purification, epidemic disease prevention, and personal hygiene protection.
journal: Chem

title: Evolution from out-of-plane to in-plane metallo-annulenes: Theoretical investigations of putative planar transition metallo-annulenes
content: The annulenes typically coordinate with transition metals to form out-of-plane metallo-annulene. Expanding the ring cavity shifts the metal into the ring core via metal–carbon σ bonds, establishing a unique structural paradigm. Herein, we systematically explore planar metallo-[n]annulenes (12 ≤ n ≤17), mapping out their spatial boundaries. By establishing a “periodic table” for in-plane metallo-annulenes, this work offers key conceptual insights to guide the rational design of novel organometallic architectures.
journal: Chem

title: El Agente Quntur: A research collaborator agent for quantum chemistry
content: Pérez-Sánchez, Zou, et al. present El Agente Quntur, a domain-specific multi-agent system that translates open-ended chemistry questions into literature-informed computational workflows. Benchmarks against a general-purpose coding agent and research-level case studies show that specialized reasoning improves workflow reliability, method selection, error recovery, and result interpretation while revealing persistent limitations in geometric reasoning and post-analysis.
journal: Chem

title: Molecular engineering of conjugated polyelectrolyte-enzyme biohybrid sheets for solar CO2 conversion
content: Integrating synthetic light-harvesting materials with enzymes offers a powerful strategy for solar CO2 conversion, yet molecular design principles governing semiconductor-enzyme interfaces remain underdeveloped. Here, we establish a molecular design framework based on metal-free conjugated polyelectrolyte photocatalyst sheets that spontaneously bind CO2-reducing enzymes. Systematic engineering of polymer side chains and backbones co-optimizes charge separation and biointerfacial chemistry, enhancing CO2 reduction activity by >100-fold. These structure-property-function relationships provide actionable principles for designing high-performance biohybrid platforms for solar chemical production.
journal: Chem

title: Catalytic atroposelective macrocyclization for constructing dominant rotors in peptides
content: A catalytic atroposelective macrocyclization strategy is developed to construct structurally tunable triazole-based dominant rotors in macrocyclic peptides. Different rotor configurations direct distinct macrocycle organizations and intramolecular interactions, leading to well-defined conformational states. This strategy enables atroposelective control in peptide macrocyclization and highlights the potential of axially chiral rotors as versatile structural elements for shaping macrocyclic architectures.
journal: Chem

title: Optically induced microwave emission from antiferromagnetically coupled heterometallic complexes
content: Optical excitation of antiferromagnetically coupled chromium(III) containing heterometallic systems leads to enhanced spin polarization and microwave emissions with chemically tunable g values. The optically generated states show long lifetimes that could be of interest in the context of quantum information processing.
journal: Chem

title: Carbometallation with alcohols: A facile strategy for olefin synthesis via deoxygenative hydroalkylation
content: Olefins are valuable intermediates for the construction of C(sp3)-rich frameworks. 1,1-Disubstituted olefins are especially privileged precursors because their unique geminal substitution pattern enables diverse, regioselective transformations. Despite this utility, 1,1-disubstituted olefins are less readily available than other olefin substitution classes, and many established syntheses require harsh conditions or specialized starting materials. The reported mild metallaphotoredox hydroalkylation couples abundant alcohols with bench-stable alkynes to access 1,1-di- and trisubstituted olefins.
journal: Chem

title: Site-selective Au(III)-mediated metalloenzyme conjugations
content: Au(III)-mediated cysteine S-arylation enables site-selective covalent modification of metalloenzymes while preserving the integrity of their active metal sites. This organometallic bioconjugation strategy establishes a blueprint for predictable metalloprotein functionalization and broader applications in chemical biology, protein engineering, and biotechnology.
journal: Chem

title: Concerted modulation of single-atom electronic structure and interfacial microenvironment for oxygen electroreduction
content: Yi et al. show that incorporating a low loading of Ru nanoparticles into Fe–N–C simultaneously tunes Fe–N4 active sites and the interfacial microenvironment. This concerted modulation improves oxygen-reduction kinetics and local oxygen transport, demonstrating that active-site chemistry and the interfacial water structure can be engineered together to enhance the practical performance of proton-exchange membrane fuel-cell catalysts.
journal: Chem

title: Ultrafast in vivo spectroscopy reveals photosynthetic energy and charge transfer under physiological conditions
content: Kumar et al. investigate the earliest light-driven steps of photosynthesis directly in living cyanobacterial cells. By resolving ultrafast energy and charge transfer in the native cellular environment, this work opens new opportunities for understanding how photosynthesis functions in vivo under physiologically relevant conditions.
journal: Chem

title: Upscaling electrosynthesis of hypervalent iodine through steady-state engineering
content: Translating organic electrosynthesis from laboratory discovery to practical manufacturing remains challenging. This study introduces steady-state engineering to maintain stable reaction environments, enabling productive and cost-effective electrosynthesis of hypervalent iodine reagents and facilitating scale-up from batch reactions to kilogram-scale continuous-flow processing and industrial demonstration.
journal: Chem

title: A K+ preloaded crown ether-containing metal-organic framework for efficient gold recovery from e-wastewater
content: A crown ether-incorporated metal−organic framework with preorganized K+ ions in the 18-crown-6 cavities enables specific recognition of [AuCl4]− through cation-assisted host−guest interactions. This design affords sensitive gold detection as well as rapid and highly selective gold adsorption, while maintaining excellent performance at ultra-trace concentrations. Moreover, the material displays excellent gold adsorption performance across a wide range of complex real-world aqueous systems, including e-wastewater, freshwater, seawater, and gold mine wastewater.
journal: Chem

title: Well-defined chiral binuclear copper catalysis in accessing trifluoromethyl amino acid derivatives
content: We report the first well-defined binuclear copper catalyst for asymmetric radical difunctionalization of alkenes, enabled by a crescent-shaped ligand that preorganizes a rigid cavity. Unlike spontaneous self-assembly, this architecture ensures uniform azide coordination and exceptional stereocontrol, thereby providing a general platform for the synthesis of chiral α-quaternary trifluoromethylated amino acids and peptides.
journal: Chem

title: Constructing chiral rotaxanes with both mechanical and macrocyclic planar chirality by enantioselective C–H activation
content: Chirality in mechanically interlocked molecules arises from threading topology, yet their enantioselective construction remains challenging. We report a cobalt-catalyzed C–H annulation that affords rotaxanes with both macrocyclic and mechanical planar chirality in excellent enantiopurity. Absolute configuration is unambiguously assigned via the second-generation crystalline sponge method, using crystallographic characterization of three-layered rotaxane-in-cage complexes.
journal: Chem

title: A minimal photoreactive metallocofactor for carbon–sulfur bond formation in small molecules and proteins
content: Structurally minimal nickel-thiolate complexes function as both light absorbers and reactive centers for photochemical carbon–sulfur bond formation. Ground- and excited-state characterization identifies mononuclear nickel-thiolate motifs as compact photoreactive cofactors whose reactivity can be tuned through nuclearity, substrate structure, and solvent environment. Guided by these structural and reactivity requirements, nickel-thiolate motifs were incorporated into proteins while retaining photochemical activity, providing a foundation for the design of artificial photoreactive metalloproteins.
journal: Chem

title: A triangle association strategy for de novo reaction discovery
content: A triangle association strategy (TAS) uses shared chemical reactants to systematically predict new reactions and overcome the limitations of traditional serendipity. Guided by a condition-correlation metric, this approach discovered six unprecedented catalytic reactions and enables efficient synthesis of structurally complex rings and macrocycles for drug discovery.
journal: Chem

title: Single-catalyst operando photoluminescence spectroscopy of perovskite quantum-dot-driven photoredox reactions
content: Spectroscopic measurements on individual catalysts during active operation remain difficult and typically necessitate specialized reaction conditions. This work presents a single-catalyst operando study of lead halide perovskite quantum dots, an emerging photocatalyst platform with exceptional electronic and chemical tunability. Traditional reactant concentration limits are overcome by immobilizing and directly interrogating individual QDs via single-particle photoluminescence spectroscopy. Thus, charging/discharging dynamics, particle-to-particle heterogeneities, activity fluctuations, and catalyst degradation can be characterized under authentic reaction conditions.
journal: Chem

title: PETase learns from LCC: Redesigning enzymatic reactivity with probability-based simulations
content: Plastic-degrading enzymes represent a promising strategy to address the global plastic waste problem, but their catalytic efficiency still falls short of industrial needs. Rather than relying on a single static structure, the authors use a probability-based simulation framework to capture the full ensemble of reactive pathways in PETase and LCCICCG, two promising candidates for biotechnological plastic recycling. These insights are translated into a rationally engineered PETase variant with improved activity, showcasing probability-guided design as a general strategy for enzyme engineering.
journal: Chem

title: Coordination-modulated 6FDA-polyimide membranes for enhanced helium molecular sieving
content: Helium is increasingly valuable, but separating it efficiently remains difficult. This work shows that metal coordination can reorganize polymer chains to create highly selective molecular pathways, thereby providing a simple strategy to improve membrane performance beyond conventional trade-offs.
journal: Chem

title: Multidentate anchoring molecule-assisted blade-coated self-assembled monolayer for scalable and stable perovskite photovoltaics
content: Achieving the scalable and controlled formation of self-assembled monolayers during blade coating remains challenging. Here, we introduce a multidentate thiol-anchoring co-adsorbate that suppresses SAM aggregation and constructs a hydrogen-bonded, hydrophilic buried interface. By coupling molecular dispersion, interfacial wettability, and stress relaxation, this strategy offers a general design principle for blade-coated, efficient, and durable perovskite photovoltaics.
journal: Chem

title: Replicating the Bohr/Haldane effect in a synthetic system
content: A synthetic molecular cage reproduces the key features of the Bohr/Haldane effect in hemoglobin. Protonation and deprotonation unfold and fold the cage framework, promoting anionic cargo uptake and release, respectively; meanwhile, anion loading and unloading reciprocally decrease and increase the acidity of the cage by several pKa units. This feature enables pH-gradient-driven directional anion transport across an organic liquid membrane.
journal: Chem

title: Protein olympiadanes
content: Mechanically interlocked proteins represent an emerging frontier in chemical topology and protein engineering. Here, we demonstrate the direct synthesis of protein olympiadanes—higher-order catenanes inspired by the Olympic rings—within living cells using a modular assembly strategy. The platform enables the construction of multiple constitutional isomers and produces exceptionally stable architectures. By providing a modular route to increasingly complex protein topologies, this work establishes a foundation for the programmable construction of mechanically interlocked proteins.
journal: Chem

title: Phosphate group-assisted interfacial proton diffusion facilitates direct ethylene electro-oxidation to ethylene glycol
content: We report that interfacial proton accumulation is the key limitation on the Faradaic efficiency (FE) of direct ethylene oxidation to ethylene glycol at industrially relevant current densities. Thus, a phytic acid-modified AgPd (AgPd-PA) electrocatalyst is designed to facilitate the diffusion of interfacial protons and accelerate the formation of ∗OH. This strategy achieves a record FE of 40.8% and a yield rate of 758.6 μmol h−1 at 100 mA cm−2 for ethylene glycol synthesis.
journal: Chem

title: Molybdenum doping enhances backbonding at neighboring iron centers in iron-sulfur clusters
content: Why is the Mo nitrogenase more adept at N2 reduction than its alternative nitrogenase counterparts (V and Fe-only)? To investigate this question, we undertook a comparative structural and spectroscopic analysis of synthetic [MoFe3S4] and [Fe4S4] clusters. We found differences in how the clusters distribute electron density, with the iron centers in the [MoFe3S4] clusters being better at backbonding to weakly π-acidic ligands. Such differences may account for the greater efficiency of the Mo nitrogenase.
journal: Chem

title: The influence of heterometals on dinitrogen binding at synthetic iron-sulfur clusters
content: Of the three nitrogenase isozymes (Mo, V, and Fe-only), the Mo nitrogenase shows the highest selectivity for N2 vs. H+ reduction. Here, we study the reduction chemistry of a series of synthetic [MFe3S4] clusters and find that only those that contain large auxiliary metals bind N2 at Fe. These results support an electronic role for “heterometals” featuring diffuse orbitals in facilitating N2 binding at neighboring Fe sites.
journal: Chem

title: Organopotassium for selective synthesis: Potassium-mediated anti-borylfunctionalization of alkynes
content: Organopotassium compounds are highly reactive organometallic species whose poor solubility and stability have long limited their synthetic applications. This study reports the potassium-mediated anti-selective difunctionalization of alkynes via reductive borylpotassiation. Reduction of alkyne with a potassium reductant in the presence of reduction-resistant trialkoxyborane results in anti-diboration. Performing the reductive borylpotassiation in flow microreactors enables the unsymmetrical borylfunctionalization of alkynes in an anti-fashion. These distinctive anti-selective difunctionalization reactions afford synthetically valuable multi-substituted alkenes, such as tamoxifen, with excellent regio- and stereoselectivity.
journal: Chem

title: An isolable nitrene radical anion as a nucleophilic open-shell nitrogen synthon
content: Nitrenes are well-known reactive intermediates used to form a variety of nitrogen-containing molecules, but their reduced radical anions have remained inaccessible under ambient temperature. Here, a persistent nitrene can be converted into an isolable radical anion that features a non-Aufbau electronic configuration. This species acts as a nucleophilic nitrogen radical that forms new N–Se, N–Si, and N–C bonds under mild conditions.
journal: Chem

title: High-performance superphane membranes for sustainable flow batteries
content: Superphane cages construct precision-engineered subnanometer channels in membranes, enabling Grotthuss-driven rapid proton conduction and size-exclusion selectivity. This design simultaneously suppresses water migration via confined supramolecular interactions, which results in a record-low capacity decay of 0.008% per cycle in acidic flow batteries.
journal: Chem

title: Direct conversion of N2 and CH4 to valuable N-containing compounds via a plasma-activated catalytic process
content: Direct co-conversion of N2 and CH4 into alkylamines and NH3 is achieved under mild conditions via a non-thermal plasma-activated catalytic process over a Ni/SiAlO catalyst. The plasma-catalysis synergy not only facilitates the activation of reactants by increasing the mean electron energy but also enables catalyst-regulated N–C and N–H coupling of adsorbed intermediates with plasma-derived reactive species. This one-step process bypasses the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch and amination cascade processes, offering a sustainable synthetic route under mild conditions.
journal: Chem

title: Foam-to-foam recycling of non-isocyanate polyurethane foams via complete revalorization of depolymerization products
content: This work introduces a chemical recycling route that converts CO2-based non-isocyanate polyurethane (NIPU) foams back into cyclic carbonate building blocks (re-5CC) for direct re-foaming. A stepwise one-pot process combines foam deconstruction and re-functionalization, reusing all major depolymerization products while avoiding intermediate purification and reducing waste. The produced re-5CCs enable second-generation foams with up to 100% recycled carbonate source, advancing practical foam-to-foam recycling for NIPU foams.
journal: Chem

title: Sequential Zn2+-H+ storage in a 2D conductive metal-organic framework for advanced aqueous zinc-ion battery
content: The conductive 2D MOF Cu3(HHTATP)2 addresses H+-induced side reactions in acidic aqueous zinc-ion batteries by enabling voltage-separated sequential Zn2+ and H+ storage. Its multi-site redox chemistry, including reversible H+-mediated amine/imine conversion at pendant amines, suppresses LDH-related interference while affording high capacity, rapid ion diffusion, and excellent rate capability.
journal: Chem

title: Actinide-actinide bonding visualized by Hirshfeld atom refinement
content: Covalency in chemical bonding is a well-established concept, but few methods experimentally measure covalency. X-ray charge density determination could be the most powerful method for visualizing chemical bonding, but its stringent requirements have prevented routine implementation. Hirshfeld atom refinement (HAR) has emerged as a more accessible approach for experimentally visualizing covalency, and here it is applied to two extreme test cases of trithorium clusters containing multi-center thorium-thorium bonding. We demonstrate excellent experimental-computational agreement, paving the way to the routine use of HAR visualization of chemical bonding.
journal: Chem

title: Triggering expeditious Zn2+ DMSO-bridged deposition through high-entropy, H2O-depleted hydrogel electrolyte for wide-temperature zinc batteries
content: The single H2O solvent system is the primary factor limiting Zn2+ deposition kinetics and a battery's operating temperature window. We reconstructed the Zn2+ solvation structure and H2O molecule hydrogen-bonding network by designing a multi-solvent system, thereby achieving expeditious deposition kinetics and broad temperature-range operation for the battery. Our work provides new insights into durable and high-rate aqueous batteries capable of operating in real-world, thermally fluctuating environments.
journal: Chem

title: Light-induced diluted CO2 capture and photoreduction
content: We synthesized a series of stable metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) composed by [FeIII2MII(μ3-O)] (abbreviated as Fe2MO) clusters, denoted as USTC-12-Fe2M (M = Mn, Co, Ni), for photocatalytic CO2 reduction in a 15% CO2 atmosphere. Remarkably, USTC-12-Fe2Mn exhibits an ultrahigh CO2-to-CO conversion rate, reaching ∼16.1 mmolCO·gcatalyst−1·h−1 with 95% CO selectivity and an apparent quantum efficiency of 2.66% under visible-light irradiation. Experimental results reveal that Fe is the real active site driving photocatalytic CO2 reduction, with the divalent metal in the cluster modulating the Fe electronic state. In situ experiments demonstrate that CO2 molecules can be readily captured by the μ3-O atom and pre-activated on Fe2MO clusters to form ∗c-CO32− intermediates under light irradiation, enabling CO2 photoreduction at low CO2 concentrations.
journal: Chem

title: Copper-catalyzed doubly enantioconvergent radical C(sp3)–P cross-coupling for the construction of P- and P,C-stereogenic centers
content: Liu and colleagues report a copper-catalyzed enantioconvergent radical C(sp³)–P cross-coupling of racemic secondary phosphine oxides and H-phosphinates with alkyl bromides in order to enable the efficient synthesis of P-stereogenic phosphorus compounds. The same catalytic platform further enables the doubly enantioconvergent construction of vicinal P,C-stereocenters from racemic H-phosphinates and racemic secondary benzyl bromides. This method provides a general and practical approach to phosphorus-centered chirality and may inspire the development of related strategies for other heteroatom-centered stereogenic systems.
journal: Chem

title: Interface engineering of Fe-based multifunctional catalysts for selective CO2 hydrogenation to C3+ alcohols
content: Highly selective hydrogenation of CO2 into higher alcohols with three or more carbon atoms remains challenging due to inherent difficulties in regulating C–C coupling of reaction intermediates. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that a well-tailored K-modified ZnZrOx–Fe5C2 interface optimizes alkyl-oxygenate coupling, enabling efficient higher alcohol synthesis with a record-high C3+ alcohol yield and excellent long-term stability. This work demonstrates great practical potential for producing value-added chemicals via CO2 hydrogenation.
journal: Chem

title: Interface-induced built-in magnetic field boosted spin exchange interactions to enable high-efficiency oxygen electrocatalysis
content: Engineered antiferromagnetic/ferromagnetic heterostructures generate an interfacial built-in magnetic field that aligns electron spins, an effect that enables external field-free control of spin-dependent oxygen electrocatalysis via rapid quantum spin exchange interactions. This strategy enhances oxygen evolution activity and reveals the critical role of spin polarization in governing reaction process; thus, it offers a general design principle for efficient energy conversion materials.
journal: Chem

title: Interfacial hydrogen-bond network regulation enables selective CO2 reduction to ethanol on copper-free electrocatalysts
content: Selective electroreduction of CO2 into ethanol—a storable fuel—has been limited almost exclusively to copper. Herein, a copper-free Ag/Cr2O3 catalyst is designed to produce ethanol with >50% faradaic efficiency at ∼160 mA/cm2 with the assistance of perchlorate. The presence of perchlorate disrupts the continuous hydrogen-bond network, thereby inhibiting the competing hydrogen evolution. The Ag–Cr asymmetric sites further stabilize the C–C coupling intermediates and lower the ethanol pathway barriers over ethylene, thus enabling selective ethanol generation.
journal: Chem

title: Programmed molecular self-organization directed by molecular Morse code
content: A system for coding transmissible information in peptides employs α- and β-amino acids, which yield strands that assemble into antiparallel β sheets if sequences match. It has been used to control conformations in hairpin peptides and to direct self-sorting in hydrogel fibers. The scheme could provide a means of information storage and transfer in the “amyloid world” hypothesis for the origin of life.
journal: Chem

title: Polymer platform for peroxynitrite detection utilizing benzopyrylium chemistry
content: Tracking reactive oxygen and nitrogen species such as peroxynitrite is key to understanding disease progression linked to oxidative stress, but existing small-molecule fluorescent probes are limited by their functional lifetimes. This polymeric design overcomes these limitations by improving stability, solubility, and biocompatibility. Further assembly into nanoparticles enables sensitive, long-lasting near-infrared imaging with a dynamic response to peroxynitrite. This work highlights how tunable polymeric designs extend probe lifetimes and enable continuous monitoring of disease-relevant chemistry in complex biological systems.

title: Biointerface‐Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria‐Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
content:
Biointerface‐customized nanomodulators (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP) enable precise mitochondrial targeting in tumors through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), in which coordinated ion interference and photothermal activation induce calcium overload, membrane potential collapse, and mitochondrial dysfunction. This organelle‐specific stress triggers immunogenic tumor cell death and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment, promoting pro‐inflammatory immune activation and enhanced antitumor immunity in vivo.








ABSTRACT
Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
content:
A laser‐induced carbothermal method is employed to synthesize high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles. The particle minimization design is proved to reduce energy loss, while the high entropy doping strategy improves voltage and capacity retention. Together, these two features contribute to outstanding electrochemical performance of the cathode material. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling.








ABSTRACT
The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg−1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

title: Ionic‐Ligand‐Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg−1 Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
An ionic‐ligand‐assisted solid polymer electrolyte is designed by integrating poly(ionic liquid) moieties into a fluorinated backbone. The cationic side chains tightly anchor FSI− anions, creating continuous, anion‐dominated channels. This reconstructs the solvation environment to enable rapid Li+ hopping, achieving outstanding conductivity, a high transference number, and robust interfacial stability in Li||NCM90 cells.








ABSTRACT
Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI− anions, creating anion‐rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li+ hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm−1) and an exceptional Li+ transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid‐state Li||LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high‐energy‐density (515 Wh kg−1) solid‐state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high‐loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm−2) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic‐ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance and high‐safety solid‐state batteries.

title: In‐Situ Self‐Evolving µ‐Sn10Bi Cross‐Interlocked Structure and Three‐in‐One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low‐Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
content:
A remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy was tailored for µ‐Sn by introducing trace µ‐Bi. The 3D interlocked Bi network formed through self‐evolution not only reinforces the electrode structure but also improves the reaction kinetics of Sn by dynamic conductivity compensation, supercontinuous Bi (104) crystal planes, and Sn/Bi heterointerface, achieving superb sodium storage performance at room/low temperatures.








ABSTRACT
Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e−/Na+ transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn10Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn10Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
content:
Remote catalytic dehydrogenation enables the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer by thermal CVD. Spatial separation of the catalyst from the growth substrate eliminates metallic residue and post‐growth processing, yielding a wafer‐scale uniform film with a random polygonal sp2‐hybridized carbon network that exhibits insulating, gate‐tunable hopping transport, enabling direct device integration.








ABSTRACT
Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp2‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: Synthesis of Ti2B2Clx MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
content:
By integrating a theoretical framework with experiments, Ti2InB2 was selectively etched with ZnCl2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti2B2Clx MBene. The In atoms are completely removed, with simultaneous incorporation of chlorine surface terminations. in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti2InB2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation, corroborated by a recently developed computational framework.








ABSTRACT
The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti2InB2 with ZnCl2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti2B2Clx MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x‐ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti2InB2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti2ZnB2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
content:
This review examines organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) through the lens of the bioelectronic interface, tracing a design hierarchy from molecular structure and electrolyte‐channel engineering to device architecture and circuit integration. Applications spanning electrophysiology, wearable and implantable sensing, and plant monitoring are discussed, alongside an outlook toward closed‐loop bioelectronic systems that sense, process, and respond within a single integrated platform.








ABSTRACT
Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
content:
A motif‐conserved aramide platform reveals how progressive organization of acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures amplifies iodine adsorption. Increasing architectural dimensionality creates more accessible, confined, and cooperative binding environments, leading to non‐additive gains in per‐motif performance, with the cage architecture delivering exceptional I3− capture under competitive aqueous conditions.








ABSTRACT
The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I3− per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro–Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
content:
Personalized hybrid nanovesicles (Atro@Carve‐NNVs) are engineered by fusing atropine‐loaded autologous tumor cell membrane vesicles with carvedilol‐loaded, NP41‐functionalized liposomes. This Atro@Carve‐NNV administration‐mediated dual neurotherapy (ADNT), prepared in close integration with prostate cancer surgical resection, simultaneously modulates sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves, remodeling neuro–immune crosstalk and chemokine network to suppress postoperative recurrence and metastasis.








ABSTRACT
The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Autonomous Discovery of Multi‐Material Metamaterials With Programmable Multimodal Thermal Responses via Reinforcement Learning
content:
A physics‐guided deep reinforcement learning framework is developed to achieve the autonomous inverse design of multi‐material thermal metamaterials. By integrating physical constraints and hybrid iterative optimization, the AI agent efficiently explores vast combinatorial design spaces from sparse data, discovering nonintuitive multi‐material architectures with programmable, coupled multimodal thermal expansion and twisting behaviors.








ABSTRACT
Inverse design deep learning models have significantly accelerated materials discovery through mapping complex structure‐property relationships. However, they remain constrained by prohibitive data demands and are limited to in‐distribution interpolation designs. Efficient out‐of‐distribution inverse design under sparse data constraints remains a critical bottleneck. Here we present an inverse design framework integrating Transformer encoder with reinforcement learning (RL) agent. By combining adaptable structural parameterization and hybrid iterative optimization, this framework efficiently navigates the complex, high‐dimensional multi‐material design landscape with extremely low data dependency (<103 samples). The inverse design framework leverages reward‐driven mechanism to autonomously evolves multi‐material architectures that achieve unseen target thermal deformation behaviors while strictly adhering to manufacturing requirements. Uniquely, the versatility of this framework is demonstrated through the realization of multiple thermal deformation targets, including near‐zero, negative, and highly anisotropic thermal expansion, as well as complex multimodal deformations. Experimental validation of fabricated structures further confirms the efficacy of our framework for accelerated on‐demand design of multi‐material functional architectures.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
content:
The strategy of host–guest recognition based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks accelerates the oxygen reduction reaction. 








ABSTRACT
Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O2. A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential (E1/2, vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
content:
ABSTRACT
The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (Cdl)‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
content:
Ultrafast laser direct writing constructs a hierarchical graphene host with adjacent Co single atoms and nanoparticles, whose electronic coupling generates a spatial adsorption‐energy gradient. This coupling homogenizes Li+ flux and thermodynamically directs dense lateral Li growth, suppressing dendritic buildup and enabling highly stable practical lithium metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
content:
Artificial cilia translate the sophisticated structure–function relationships of biological cilia into dynamic and multifunctional systems. This review highlights advances in their biomimetic design, fabrication, actuation, and emerging applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. Furthermore, future opportunities for developing more adaptive, efficient and versatile ciliary systems are also outlined.








ABSTRACT
Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
content:
Conventional postsurgical cardiac monitoring relies primarily on electrical signals, which may provide limited insight into myocardial mechanical function. Here, we introduce a passive, machine learning‐integrated platform based on a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch containing high‐remanence α′′‐Fe₁₆N2 particles, which is attached to the epicardium during open‐heart surgery. The implanted MPM patch generates magnetic field variations during cardiac motion, which are captured by an external magnetometer. After signal preprocessing and standardization, an XGBoost regression model converts the measured multi‐axis magnetic field vectors into 3D spatial coordinates of the patch. The estimated cardiac position is then differentiated to derive myocardial velocity profiles, enabling extraction of characteristic systolic and diastolic velocity parameters. In vivo validation demonstrates the capability of the platform to resolve cardiac mechanical dynamics, while 12‐week implantation further supports its long‐term biocompatibility. This passive and untethered sensing strategy provides a foundation for repeated postoperative assessment of cardiac mechanical function.








ABSTRACT
We report a machine learning (ML)‐augmented magnetic sensing system for real‐time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″‐Fe16N2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML‐based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical‐grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real‐time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
content:
Intermetallic Ni–Al chemistry enables aluminum incorporation beyond surface‐limited deposition, while a high‐surface‐area Ni powder architecture provides the kinetics required for reversible alloying. This thermodynamic–kinetic coupling promotes bulk Al incorporation and enables durable aqueous aluminum batteries, delivering long‐term symmetric‐cell stability, 4000‐cycle coin‐cell operation, and stable pouch‐cell performance.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous aluminum‐based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic‐anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni–Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high‐surface‐area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface‐limited deposition. The resulting Al‐alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge‐transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric‐cell operation and long‐duration full‐cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low‐cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm−2. When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm−2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni‐assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al‐containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
content:
A nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer is designed as a triplet sensitizer in organic photovoltaics. The triplet polymer enables a direct transfer of triplet excitons from its T1 state to i‐EX state of the host blend, which is a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway. The extra triplet excitons then dissociate into free charges to contribute photocurrents, leading to an efficiency of 20.37%.








ABSTRACT
Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: Ultra‐Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
content:
Coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with ultrahigh antiphase boundary energy are embedded in ferromagnetic Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy. This strategy boosts strengthening efficiency of nonmagnetic elements, realizing concurrent excellent soft magnetic and mechanical properties and offering a route for advanced soft magnetic alloy design.








ABSTRACT
Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non‐ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m2) into the ferromagnetic face‐centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non‐magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am2/kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe‐Si and Fe‐Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high‐performance soft magnetic alloys.

title: Closed‐Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
content:
This graphical abstract illustrates the closed‐loop bioelectronics paradigm, integrating functional materials, biosensing and actuation interfaces, intelligent system architectures, and clinical translation. At its core, the cycle of Sense–Analyze–Act highlights autonomous therapeutic feedback, showcasing how advanced materials, adaptive electronics, and real‐world applications converge to enable next‐generation bioelectronic healthcare solutions.








ABSTRACT
Closed‐loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed‐schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real‐time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed‐loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed‐loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof‐of‐concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next‐generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.
